text:
Maya Patel: TL;DR — proposing a step-based canary schedule for model v4 rollout with explicit hold windows and runtime guards. Draft below, need API shape + console UX feedback.

Diego Torres: prefer keep it simple. are fractional percents required? integer steps (1,5,10...) seems easier for routing and telemetry aggregation.

Priya Shah: fractional is fine from the router side (we already support weighted backends), but analytics + billing need to treat tiny fractions carefully. console should show absolute request counts not just percents.

Luke Kim: big ask: add hard guards for latency/errors and an opt-in auto-rollback. experience shows p95 spikes right after step changes. also we should expose a "hold_on_cpu" guard for infra.

Maya Patel: agreed on guards. initial draft:
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  type: canary
  steps:
    - traffic_percent: 1
      hold: 30m
    - traffic_percent: 5
      hold: 30m
    - traffic_percent: 20
      hold: 1h
    - traffic_percent: 50
      hold: 2h
    - traffic_percent: 100
      hold: 0m
  guards:
    max_error_rate_p99: 0.5%  # immediate rollback if exceeded during hold window
    max_p95_latency_ms: 200
    max_cpu_percent: 85
  auto_rollback: true
  evaluation_window: 5m
  tag_header: X-Canary-Group
  seed_percentage: 0.1  # small seeded fraction for internal test accounts
```

Priya Shah: a couple notes: 1) seed_percentage as decimal is ok, but be explicit in API docs about unit (0.1 = 0.1%). maybe call it seed_millis or seed_permyriad? 2) evaluation_window interacts with hold — do we average metrics across the whole hold or only last N minutes?

Diego Torres: API-wise I'd rather traffic_percent be a number 0-100 (float allowed). prefer percent decimals saved as floats in DB. avoid ambiguous units. for docs: show examples.

Luke Kim: For UX, console should show a timeline: steps as bars, real-time metrics overlay (p95, error, CPU). also expose a "force-advance" and a manual "pause" button with confirmation.

Maya Patel: Good calls. For evaluation semantics: propose rolling window = evaluation_window (e.g., 5m) inside each hold. guards are evaluated continuously; if threshold breached for >evaluation_window we trigger rollback. That prevents transient flaps.

Priya Shah: Sounds right. Also add a post-step quality check hook to run small automated prompts/evals against a held sample to detect semantic regressions before moving on. metadata: evaluate_quality: true, sample_size: 50.

Luke Kim: re: fractional percents — we must ensure rollout metrics avoid integer rounding issues. e.g., at low traffic zones 1% of 10rps is tiny. console should show both percent + absolute requests per minute.

deploy-bot: Deploy bot: started canary rollout for model:v4 -> canary id c-20240416-9 at 1718543210 on staging :rocket:

infra-bot: Infra alert: noticed CPU climb at ~step 3 to 82% on pool-gateway-3 (link: https://metrics/reports/abc123) :eyes:

Diego Torres: thanks infra-bot. propose adding dynamic hold extension: if infra CPU > threshold, extend current hold by +30m up to a max. otherwise we get forced step advance and thrash.

Maya Patel: nice. update policy with optional "extend_on_guard" block. also adding an API field:
```json
"extend_on_guard": { "cpu": { "threshold": 80, "extend_minutes": 30, "max_extensions": 3 } }
```

Priya Shah: small API debate — do we accept both a high-level "canary_policy" object (what we've sketched) and a low-level "steps" array? I'd prefer one canonical shape to avoid drift.

Diego Torres: single canonical shape makes sense. but keep helper SDK builders for common defaults.

Luke Kim: I'll mock the console UX with the new canonical shape and include tooltips for each guard and an inline simulation showing estimated qps per step. I'll push a PR by EOD.

Maya Patel: action items:
- Priya: write integration tests for guard evaluation + quality hook (assign)
- Luke: console mock + force-advance/pause UX PR
- Diego: update rollout API spec to require canonical shape and explicit percent units
- Maya: add doc PR with examples and YAML/JSON snippets

Priya Shah: OK will do tests. also will add a small e2e that seeds internal test accounts via header routing.

Diego Torres: one last product thought: add an optional "staged-traffic-routing" mode where certain user segments (by account id or header) can be excluded/included at each step for targeted A/B experiments. not today but leave field in schema.

Maya Patel: noted. leaving schema extensible. if no objections I'll update the swagger/spec and open a draft PR tonight.

Luke Kim: :+1: from me.

Priya Shah: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy bot: canary c-20240416-9 progressed to 5% at 1718543410

Maya Patel: ok closing here. will follow up in PR with final schema. thanks everyone.
